info.title: Operation Borderless
info.description:
A cross-border stablecoin payment sandbox: multi-currency wallets, simulated deposits,
cross-currency swaps, wallet-to-wallet transfers and transaction history.

### Money is never a JSON number
Every amount crosses this boundary as a **decimal string**. `JSON.parse('{"amount":0.1}')`
already holds an IEEE-754 double before any server code runs, so a number here would be
corrupted in transit. Internally amounts are integer counts of a currency’s minor units.

### Precision is per currency
An amount with more decimal places than its currency admits is **rejected, not rounded**.
`cXAF` has 0 decimals — the Central African CFA franc has no subunit in circulation — so
`"100.50"` is not a representable amount. `GET /currencies` publishes the precision of each.

### Conversions floor
A converted amount is floored to the destination currency’s precision, so the system can
never credit more value than it debited. A conversion that would round to zero is rejected.

### Retries are safe
The three money-moving endpoints require an `Idempotency-Key`. Retrying with the same key
returns the original response rather than moving money twice; reusing a key with a
different body is rejected. Responses carry `Idempotency-Replayed`.

### Errors
Every failure returns the same envelope. Branch on `error.code`, never on the status alone —
several distinct conditions return 422. `error.retryable` says whether retrying the
identical request could succeed.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS",
    "message": "Insufficient funds",
    "details": { "currency": "USDx", "requested": "50.000000", "available": "10.000000" },
    "requestId": "01a186de-eff5-7145-aec9-fef34adc48d9",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

### Getting started
1. `POST /v1/wallets` — creates a wallet and returns a token pair.
2. Paste the `accessToken` into **Authorize** above.
3. `POST /v1/deposits`, then `/v1/swaps` or `/v1/transfers`.

walletId.description: The wallet these tokens authenticate. Needed as `toWalletId` by a sender.

accessToken.description: Bearer token for all authenticated endpoints.

refreshToken.description: Used once at POST /auth/tokens/refresh, then rotated.
The refresh token issued alongside the current access token.

from.description: Currency code. The valid set is whatever GET /currencies returns.

rate.description: Units of `to` per 1 unit of `from`, as a decimal string.

asOf.description: When the underlying rates were last refreshed upstream.

source.description: Where these rates came from, in descending order of freshness: `live` - just fetched from the provider. `cached` - a live fetch, served from Redis within its TTL. `stale` - the provider is unavailable; last-known-good from the database. `fallback` - the provider is unavailable and no snapshot exists; committed static table.

degraded.description: True only when the live provider could not be reached, so `source` is `stale` or `fallback`. A `cached` rate inside its TTL is the normal operating mode and is not reported as degraded.

peg.description: ISO-4217 code of the fiat currency tracked 1:1.

decimals.description: Decimal places this currency admits. An amount with more is rejected.

email.description: Email address. Either this or `phone` is required. Stored lower-cased.

phone.description: Mobile number in E.164 format. Either this or `email` is required.

password.description: At least 12 characters. Hashed with scrypt; never stored or logged in clear.

amount.description: Balance as a decimal string at the currency precision. A string, not a number, because JSON numbers are IEEE-754 doubles and would corrupt the value before a client could read it.

usdEquivalent.description: Equivalent in USDx at the current rate.

balances.description: One entry per supported currency, including zero balances.

totalUsdEquivalent.description: Total value of every balance, in USDx. Each leg is floored independently, so the total is never reported higher than its true value.

totalCurrency.description: The currency the total is denominated in.

ratesAsOf.description: When the rates used for the USD conversions were last refreshed upstream.

ratesSource.description: Which tier of the FX chain priced this response. Anything other than `live` means the live provider was unavailable and a cached, stale or static rate was used.

tokens.description: Token pair for the new wallet, so creation and first use are a single round trip. `walletId` here is what another wallet needs as `toWalletId` to send you money.

balances.description: One entry per supported currency, including zero balances.

totalUsdEquivalent.description: Total value of every balance, in USDx. Each leg is floored independently, so the total is never reported higher than its true value.

totalCurrency.description: The currency the total is denominated in.

ratesAsOf.description: When the rates used for the USD conversions were last refreshed upstream.

ratesSource.description: Which tier of the FX chain priced this response. Anything other than `live` means the live provider was unavailable and a cached, stale or static rate was used.

amount.description: Amount as an unsigned decimal string, at most as precise as the currency allows. A string rather than a number so no floating-point rounding can occur in transit.

direction.description: DEBIT when this movement left the calling wallet, CREDIT when it arrived. A single transfer therefore reads as sent to one party and received by the other, without being duplicated.

sourceAmount.description: Amount debited, as a decimal string.

destAmount.description: Amount credited, as a decimal string.

rate.description: Rate applied, as units of destCurrency per 1 sourceCurrency.

rateSource.description: Which tier of the FX chain supplied the rate. `pegged` means a same-currency movement, which needs no provider at all.

rateAsOf.description: When the applied rate was last refreshed upstream.

toCurrency.description: Currency to credit. Must differ from fromCurrency.

amount.description: Amount as an unsigned decimal string, at most as precise as the currency allows. A string rather than a number so no floating-point rounding can occur in transit. Denominated in fromCurrency.

toWalletId.description: The receiving wallet. The sender is always the token holder, so there is no fromWalletId.

currency.description: Currency to debit from the sender.

toCurrency.description: Currency to credit to the receiver. Defaults to `currency`. When they differ the amount is converted at the current rate and both legs are recorded.

amount.description: Amount as an unsigned decimal string, at most as precise as the currency allows. A string rather than a number so no floating-point rounding can occur in transit. Denominated in currency.

id.description: The transaction this row belongs to.

entryId.description: The ledger entry itself. A cross-currency swap produces two rows in one wallet's statement -- a debit in the source currency and a credit in the destination -- sharing one transaction id but with distinct entry ids.

direction.description: DEBIT when money left this wallet, CREDIT when it arrived.

amount.description: Magnitude of this row, as a decimal string.

balanceAfter.description: This wallet's balance in this currency immediately after the row was applied.

counterpartyWalletId.description: The other wallet, for a transfer. Null for deposits and swaps.

rate.description: Rate applied to the whole transaction.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.

requestId.description: Correlation id, matching the `requestId` the client saw in the error envelope.
